newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes stronger on rise in dlr supply.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes stronger on rise in dlr supply.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed around 2,220-2,250 per dollar, stronger from midday's 2,350-2,450 and 2,500-2,550 at the opening, as foreign currency supply rose in anticipation of a continuing lev rise, dealers said.
"Dollar supply heavily topped demand, and the lev advanced by around 450 from yesterday's close," a commercial bank dealer said. The lev closed around 2,660-2,720 per dollar on Tuesday.

Expectations increased of new lev gains after finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said on Tuesday the lev might rise to 2,000 if banks refrained from speculatively pressuring the lev when large final clients were bidding for dollars.
Dealers said big client dollar buying was not expected to push the lev down if clients like energy importers directly contacted banks with ample dollar liquidity.
Some dealers said several large state-owned banks might have entered an agreement for boosting the lev this week but declined to elaborate.
The lev traded around 2,800 per dollar on Monday. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
